solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Waiting without complaint for a game

definitions.meaning: calm forbearance while waiting is the virtue of the long-suffering
the card game for one player, known in the US as solitaire

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the virtue of uncomplaining endurance and the British name for solitaire card games.

clue.text: Took off and levelled out

definitions.meaning: removed wood with a carpenter's tool
made a surface flat and smooth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' reads as an aircraft leaving the ground; here it is shaving wood away.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's plane both removes thin shavings and smooths a board flat.

clue.text: Trial meant to determine will

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: to determine is to settle or fix, here how the letters of the word before it are arranged

explanation.surface: A trial is held to decide what a will means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to determine' loosely rearranges MEANT into AMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: Worker encountered me coming up first

indicators.note: first puts that reversed piece ahead of the other
coming up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
met means encountered

explanation.surface: A worker met me as I came up first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' suggests a labourer; it is the insect, by a dialect name used in East Anglia and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: An emmet is a dialect word for an ant, the classic worker insect.

clue.text: Song many play badly in this way

parts.note: C, the Roman hundred, stands for many

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the word are played wrongly

parts.note: so means in this way

explanation.surface: Many people play a song badly in this fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Using C for 'many' is a crossword liberty: the Roman hundred stands for a large number.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean song style from Trinidad.

clue.text: Pays out for odds and ends

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pays money for a pile of odds and ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds and ends' reads as one phrase for bits and pieces, but splits: the odds are the starting price in British horse-race betting.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money is to pay it out, so one who spends pays out.

clue.text: Share pusher

parts.note: share looks financial, but a ploughshare is the blade of a plough, pushed by its driver

explanation.walkthrough: In a financial paper 'Share pusher' suggests a stockbroker; the share is a ploughshare.
explanation.definitionFit: The farmhand guiding a plough drives its blade, the share, through the soil.

clue.text: Hospital situated in pleasant nook

indicators.note: situated in puts the abbreviation for hospital inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital sits in a pleasant little corner.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or small hollow, like a nook.

clue.text: The evening air?

parts.note: air is not the atmosphere but a tune, sung at evening beneath a window

explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' suggests cool night breeze; it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: This song is traditionally sung by a lover at night under a beloved's window.

clue.text: Group together competent to contain return of disorder

indicators.note: to contain says the word for competent holds the other piece within it

parts.note: competent means able

indicators.note: return of means the word for disorder is read backwards

parts.note: a disorder is a mess

explanation.surface: A capable team gathers together to bring a renewed outbreak of chaos under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group together' is a verb here, to gather, not a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To assemble is to bring or come together as a group.

clue.text: Possibly score a hundred in popular game

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters given are only one possible arrangement of them

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: In a popular game you might well score a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges SCORE plus C.
explanation.definitionFit: Association football, the world's most widely followed sport, is also called by this name.

clue.text: But it's no aspersion on the score

definitions.text: But it's no aspersion on the score

parts.words: But it's no aspersion on the score
parts.note: an aspersion is an insult, but on a musical score the same word is the curved mark joining notes

explanation.walkthrough: The word means an insult; on a score of music it is a curved line telling the player to join notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both a slander and a curved mark in music binding notes together.

clue.text: It's nice to enforce payment

definitions.meaning: nice in its old sense of precise or finely accurate
to demand and obtain money due, as a tax collector does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' here is not pleasant but its older meaning, precise, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both precise, the old sense of nice, and the verb meaning to demand payment forcibly.

clue.text: Fence given new colour

parts.note: a pale is a stake in a fence, or the fence itself
green means new or inexperienced

explanation.surface: A fence is repainted in a fresh colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' just joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This light shade of the colour of grass is a named colour.

clue.text: Breaks a leg, has to play on without pause

indicators.note: breaks says the letters of the two words beside it are broken up and reset

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone breaks a leg but has to keep performing without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break a leg' is the theatre's good-luck wish, which steers toward performing on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this instruction means play smoothly, with the notes joined and no gap between them.

clue.text: Asking out?

parts.note: asking out reads as a date, but in cricket the fielders ask the umpire to give the batter out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket fielders appeal, shouting 'Howzat?', asking the umpire to give a batter out; asking someone out also suggests being attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Appealing means making an appeal or request, as cricket fielders do for a dismissal.

clue.text: Having made a withdrawal, go into the red

indicators.note: into places the word for go inside the other word

parts.note: the red is taken as the word red
to go is to move

explanation.surface: Taking money out of the bank pushes the account into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go into the red' is a phrase for running up an overdraft, which hides that the pieces are split differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Something removed has been taken away or withdrawn.

clue.text: Famous trumpet piece? Not impressed

definitions.meaning: impressed in the sense of forced into service, as by a press gang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not impressed' looks like unmoved; it means not press-ganged, so serving freely.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a solo organ or trumpet piece and means done freely without compulsion.

clue.text: About fifty vie to be perfect

indicators.note: about says the word for vie goes round the numeral

parts.note: to vie is to compete
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: About fifty people compete to be flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: COMPETE goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete means whole and total, as perfect does in 'a perfect stranger'.

clue.text: A short month to work one finds, in the main

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation of October
an opus is a work, especially a musical one

explanation.surface: Someone finds a brief month's work at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is the old poetic word for the sea, where this creature is found.
explanation.definitionFit: The eight-armed mollusc lives in the sea, and 'the main' is a literary word for the ocean.

clue.text: He's not blind to the future

definitions.text: He's not blind to the future

parts.words: He's not blind to the future
parts.note: not blind to suggests merely aware, but it describes one who sees what is coming

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'not blind to' usually means aware of; here it is literal sight of the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet or visionary is called one who sees ahead.

clue.text: It declines to afford illumination

parts.note: declines reads as refuses, but here it means grows shorter as it burns down giving light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' seems to mean refuses to give light; really the thing shrinks as it gives light.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax light shortens steadily as it burns, so it literally declines while lighting a room.

clue.text: Foreign money invested in sugar crop and pepper

indicators.note: invested in puts the currency inside the crop, as money is put into a venture

parts.note: sugar cane is grown for sugar
the yen is the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Foreign capital is put into sugar plantations and pepper growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' fits the money surface while signalling that one piece is put inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a hot red chilli pepper, ground as a spice.

clue.text: Test gold before transaction

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a deal is a transaction

explanation.surface: Gold is tested before a sale goes through.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as OR comes from heraldry, where it names the gold tincture.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a trying experience, a severe test of endurance.

clue.text: Injured hip not long ago, in pursuit

indicators.note: injured says the letters of the next word are knocked out of shape

parts.note: lately means not long ago

explanation.surface: Someone hurt a hip recently while chasing after something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' rearranges HIP into PHI; 'pursuit' is a hobby, not a chase.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamp collecting is a hobby, and a pursuit is a pastime one follows.

clue.text: Fall into part of the main current

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone falls into part of the main current of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a debt or penalty is to fall into it, bringing it on oneself.

clue.text: Vessel found in the kitchen bin?

definitions.meaning: a large passenger ship sailing a regular route
the plastic bag lining a rubbish bin

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large passenger ship and the plastic bag that lines a rubbish bin.

clue.text: Afterwards? Dead right!

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone checks a fact later and finds it exactly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead right' looks like one phrase meaning completely right; split, it gives LATE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a subsequent time, which is what afterwards means.

clue.text: With a new clue I'd get this mathematician

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone says a reworded clue will reveal a famous mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLUEID.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek geometer of Alexandria wrote the Elements, the founding text of geometry.

clue.text: Start to teach

definitions.meaning: to begin or set something going
to instruct someone in the basics of a subject or the rites of a group

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to set going and to introduce someone to knowledge or a society's secrets.

clue.text: Wild anger to a point is still anger

indicators.note: wild says the letters of the next word run out of order

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Anger that is wild, pushed to a point, is still anger.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word both closes the surface and serves as the definition; the first 'anger' is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, so the verb means to anger.

clue.text: Double-crossing woman taking on two men

parts.note: Bet is a short form of the name Elizabeth
Ray is a man's name
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: A two-timing woman takes up with two men at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking on' just joins BET to the two names.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-crossing someone is betraying them, so the noun is a synonym.
